body.summary: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts: ChatPanelHostDeps.queue?: (runner) => ChatQueueWorker builds this window's worker over queueRunner. sendTyped(session, text, files) is the one send path for the webview's submit-turn and the attachment submit (submitTurn): with a worker it enqueues ('typed', attachments as refs; a draft chat is saved first) and does not call supersedeQueuedApprovals, so the running turn and its waiting cards are untouched; a refused enqueue (full/busy/unavailable) posts the queue's note as an informational chat message; without a worker it supersedes the waiting requests and starts the turn directly as before. drainExternal waits while this window's worker runs a queued message. The host's dispose disposes the worker. turn-lifecycle.ts: busy() stays true while a start waits in the chain (tracked by its epoch, so a start dropped by stop/detach/invalidate no longer counts). Tests: the two named tests in chat-queue-routing.test.ts over a real queue file and worker (the first also checks a refused message's note); the host tests that pinned newest-wins at the host (:138, :5018, :5455) are rewritten with their old titles noted; the chat-panel and protocol suites pass 175/175 and the lifecycle suite 32/32; the other listed tests (:1318, :2854, :4745, :5302) run on the no-queue path and pass unchanged. Mutations: dropping the queue routing, the stop flag, 'turn-running', the refusal note, or answering the cards before enqueueing each failed the tests. Plugin typecheck clean. Follow-up after the gate's first refusal: chat-panel.test.ts gains tempQueue() and runs the Stop test (was :2854) with a queue: Stop ends the running message (failed 'stopped by the user', its CLI never started) and later messages all run in order, none replaced; attachHarness takes a queue, and a new test 'host: with the queue, a submit with blank text and an attachment leaves the waiting cards as they are, waits, and runs once they are decided' asserts the cards stay (HLD: :4745 'changes to assert the card stays'); the original :4745 test is kept, marked as the no-queue fallback's rule. The chat-panel, routing and runner suites pass 168/168.
